# Westbrook High U.S. History Lesson Plan: Women's Suffrage
Grade 10 • 04/20/2026 • Teacher: Rosa Haddad

## Lesson at a glance
- Class: 24 students, 50 minutes
- Learning target: Students will explain how organizing and constitutional change contributed to women gaining the right to vote.
- Materials: timeline handout, excerpts from Susan B. Anthony's 1873 speech and the 19th Amendment, projector, exit slips
- Prior-reading check: 17 students selected the newspaper account as easier to understand; 7 selected the speech excerpt.

## Sequence
- 0–5 minutes: Display the question, "How does a movement turn a demand into law?" Students write a two-sentence prediction.
- 5–12 minutes: Review the timeline. The 19th Amendment was ratified on August 26, 1920, and certified on August 26, 1920. Discuss the difference between ratification and certification.
- 12–22 minutes: Lecture on suffrage organizing, including the Seneca Falls Convention of 1848 and the campaign for a constitutional amendment.
- 22–37 minutes: In pairs, annotate both excerpts. Mark one claim, one piece of evidence, and one difference in purpose or audience.
- Since 17 of 24 students found the speech excerpt easier, begin the paired analysis with the speech and use the newspaper account as the scaffold.
- 37–45 minutes: Each pair shares one evidence-based comparison. Brandon Kim records claims on the board; Victor Ferreira invites students who have not spoken to contribute.
- 45–50 minutes: Exit slip: name one organizing strategy and explain how the 19th Amendment changed voting rights. Collect slips at the door.

## Checks and follow-up
- Success criterion: Exit slip identifies a strategy and accurately connects the amendment to voting rights.
- Review slips before the next class; reteach ratification versus certification if that distinction is confused.
- If a student needs clarification during discussion, Rosa Haddad will restate the prompt and allow a brief written response before sharing.
